name: War of the First Coalition
description: First attempt by a coalition of European monarchies to defeat Revolutionary France, ended by the Treaty of Campo Formio in 1797.

name: War of the Second Coalition
description: Second coalition war against Revolutionary France, fought in Italy, Switzerland, Holland, Egypt and at sea; ended by the treaties of Lunéville and Amiens.

name: War of the Fifth Coalition
description: Austria's 1809 war against Napoleonic France and its German allies, decided at Wagram.

name: Finnish War
description: Russia's conquest of Finland from Sweden during the Napoleonic Wars; Finland became a Russian grand duchy.

name: War in the Vendée
description: Royalist and Catholic counter-revolutionary uprising in western France, crushed with great loss of civilian life.

name: Irish Rebellion of 1798
description: United Irishmen rising against British rule, supported by a small French landing, defeated at Vinegar Hill and Ballinamuck.

name: Wars of the Three Kingdoms
description: Interlinked civil wars in England, Scotland and Ireland, including the English Civil War, the Bishops' Wars and the Irish Confederate Wars.

name: Second Northern War
description: Sweden's war against Poland–Lithuania, Russia, Denmark, Brandenburg and the Habsburgs, including the Swedish Deluge in Poland.

name: Central American national wars (1823–1907)
description: Civil and inter-state wars among the Central American republics after independence, from the Federal Republic's civil wars to the Honduran–Nicaraguan conflicts of 1907.

name: First Carlist War
description: Spanish civil war between supporters of the infante Carlos and the liberal regency of Isabella II, fought mainly in the Basque Country, Navarre and the Maestrazgo.

name: Second Carlist War
description: Minor Carlist rising in Catalonia (the War of the Matiners).

name: Third Carlist War
description: Last Carlist rising, in the Basque Country, Navarre and Catalonia, ended by the fall of Estella in 1876 (Jaques counts it as the second).

name: Franco-Dutch War
description: Louis XIV's war against the Dutch Republic and its allies Spain, the Empire and Brandenburg; England fought alongside France until 1674.

name: First Anglo-Dutch War
description: Naval war between the Commonwealth of England and the Dutch Republic over trade and the Navigation Acts.

name: Second Anglo-Dutch War
description: Naval war between England and the Dutch Republic, ended by the Treaty of Breda after the Dutch raid on the Medway.

name: Wars of the Crusader states
description: Two centuries of warfare between the Latin states of Outremer and their Muslim neighbours, from the aftermath of the First Crusade to the fall of Acre.

name: Conquests of Genghis Khan
description: Genghis Khan's campaigns against the Western Xia, the Jin dynasty, the Qara Khitai and the Khwarazmian Empire.

name: Wars of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms
description: Wars among the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of the Heptarchy and against the Britons, until Wessex's supremacy under Egbert.

name: Anglo-Saxon conquest of Britain
description: Germanic settlement and conquest of lowland Britain against the Romano-British, as recorded in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

name: First War of Scottish Independence
description: Scotland's war against Edward I and Edward II, from Wallace's rising to Bruce's victory at Bannockburn and the Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton.

name: Second War of Scottish Independence
description: Edward Balliol's and Edward III's attempts to subjugate Scotland, ended by the Treaty of Berwick.

name: Byzantine–Sasanian wars
description: Wars between the Eastern Roman Empire and Sasanian Persia from the Anastasian War to Heraclius's victory in 628.

name: Roman–Sasanian wars
description: Wars between Rome and the Sasanian Empire from Ardashir I to Julian's failed invasion of 363.

name: Mughal–Sikh wars
description: Conflicts between the Sikh gurus and their followers and the Mughal Empire, from Guru Hargobind to the execution of Banda Singh Bahadur.

name: Ottoman–Hungarian wars (1366–1526)
description: Wars between the Kingdom of Hungary and the expanding Ottoman Empire, from Louis I to the catastrophe at Mohács.

name: Early Islamic civil wars
description: Civil wars of the early caliphate, from the Ridda wars through the First, Second and Third Fitnas to the Abbasid consolidation.

name: Second Italian War of Independence
description: Franco-Sardinian war against Austria (Magenta, Solferino) followed by Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand.

name: First Italian War of Independence
description: Piedmont-Sardinia's war against Austria during the revolutions of 1848, ended by Radetzky's victory at Novara.

name: Third Italian War of Independence
description: Italy's war against Austria alongside Prussia, which gained Venetia despite defeats at Custoza and Lissa.

name: Hotaki–Safavid wars
description: Rebellion of the Ghilzai Afghans of Kandahar under Mirwais Hotak, their conquest of Safavid Persia in 1722, and Nader Shah's reconquest ending with the fall of Kandahar.

name: Early medieval Indian dynastic wars
description: Wars among the Indian dynasties of the early medieval period, including the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj and the Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Pandya rivalries.

name: Ottoman–Persian wars
description: Series of wars between the Ottoman Empire and Safavid, Afsharid and Qajar Persia from Chaldiran (1514) to the Treaty of Erzurum (1823).

name: Persian wars of succession after Nader Shah
description: Struggles among the Afsharid, Zand and Qajar contenders for Persia after the assassination of Nader Shah, ending with Agha Mohammad Khan's consolidation.

name: Herero Wars
description: German colonial war against the Herero and Nama in South West Africa, accompanied by genocide.

name: Colombian civil wars of the 19th century
description: Recurring civil wars between liberals and conservatives in Colombia (New Granada) after the dissolution of Gran Colombia.

name: Scanian War
description: Danish–Swedish war for Scania fought alongside the Franco-Dutch War; Brandenburg defeated Sweden at Fehrbellin.

name: Military campaigns of Muhammad
description: Battles and expeditions of the early Muslim community against the Meccan Quraysh and Arab tribes, from Badr to the conquest of Mecca.

name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
description: Japan's seizure of Manchuria after the Mukden Incident, followed by the creation of Manchukuo and the Rehe campaign.

name: Wars of the Second Triumvirate
description: Roman civil wars from Mutina and Philippi through the Perusine and Sicilian wars to Actium.

name: Roman–Gallic wars
description: Wars between Rome and the Gauls from the sack of Rome (390 BC) through the Cisalpine campaigns to Caesar's conquest.

name: Cimbrian War
description: Rome's war against the migrating Cimbri and Teutones, decided by Marius at Aquae Sextiae and Vercellae.

name: Civil wars of the Tetrarchy
description: Wars among the rival Roman emperors after Diocletian's abdication, ending with Constantine's sole rule.

name: Late Roman civil wars (337–394)
description: Civil wars of the Constantinian and Valentinianic dynasties, including Magnentius, Procopius, Magnus Maximus and Eugenius.

name: Crisis of the Third Century
description: Half-century of usurpations, civil wars and invasions in the Roman Empire between the death of Severus Alexander and the accession of Diocletian.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
aliases: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Civil wars, usurpations and barbarian settlements that dissolved the Western Roman Empire.

name: Year of the Five Emperors
description: Civil wars after the murder of Commodus, won by Septimius Severus over Pescennius Niger and Clodius Albinus.

name: Year of the Four Emperors
description: Civil war of AD 69 among Galba, Otho, Vitellius and Vespasian.

name: Caucasian War
description: Russia's conquest of the North Caucasus against the Circassians and the imamate of Shamil in Chechnya and Dagestan.

name: Wars of the Spring and Autumn period
aliases: Wars of China's Spring and Autumn Era
description: Wars among the states of Zhou China during the Spring and Autumn period.

name: First Peloponnesian War
description: War between Athens and Sparta's allies, chiefly Corinth, ended by the Thirty Years' Peace.

name: Wars of the Sixteen Kingdoms
aliases: Wars of the Sixteen Kingdoms Era
description: Wars among the short-lived states of northern China after the fall of the Western Jin.

name: Wars of the Western Han dynasty
description: Military campaigns of the Western Han, including the wars against the Xiongnu and the expeditions to Central Asia.

name: Wars of the Eastern Han dynasty
description: Campaigns of the Eastern Han, from Guangwu's reunification to the frontier wars against the Xiongnu, Qiang and the Trung sisters' revolt.

name: Polish–Russian War of 1792
description: Russian invasion to overturn the Constitution of 3 May, leading to the Second Partition of Poland.

name: Kościuszko Uprising
description: Polish–Lithuanian rising against Russia and Prussia, crushed at Maciejowice and followed by the Third Partition.

name: Bar Confederation
description: Polish noble confederation fighting Russian influence and King Stanisław August; its defeat preceded the First Partition.

name: Afghan war of succession (1863–1869)
description: Civil war among the sons of Dost Mohammad Khan after his death at Herat, won by Sher Ali Khan.

name: Durrani wars of succession
description: Fratricidal wars among the sons of Timur Shah Durrani that broke up the Durrani Empire and brought the Barakzai to power.

name: Byzantine–Ottoman wars
description: Wars between the declining Byzantine Empire and the rising Ottomans, from Bapheus to the fall of Constantinople.

name: Mughal wars of succession
description: Rebellions and succession wars among Mughal princes, including the war of 1657–1659 won by Aurangzeb and the struggles after his death.

name: Kievan Rus' wars of succession
description: Wars among the Rurikid princes for Kiev after the deaths of Vladimir the Great and Yaroslav the Wise.

name: Northern Seven Years' War
description: War between Sweden and a coalition of Denmark–Norway, Lübeck and Poland for supremacy in the Baltic.

name: Russo-Persian War (1804–1813)
description: War over the Caucasus ended by the Treaty of Gulistan, which ceded Georgia, Dagestan and much of Azerbaijan to Russia.

name: Russo-Persian War (1826–1828)
description: Qajar Persia's attempt to recover the Caucasus, ended by the Treaty of Turkmenchay.

name: Maccabean Revolt
description: Jewish revolt led by Judas Maccabeus against the Seleucid Empire.

name: Wars in Lombardy
description: Wars between Venice, Florence and Milan for northern Italy, ended by the Peace of Lodi.

name: Cossack uprisings against Poland–Lithuania
description: Series of Cossack rebellions (Kosiński, Nalyvaiko, Fedorovych, Pavliuk) preceding the Khmelnytsky Uprising.

name: Austro-Turkish War (1663–1664)
description: Ottoman invasion of Habsburg Hungary defeated at Saint Gotthard; ended by the Peace of Vasvár.

name: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718)
description: Habsburg war against the Ottomans won by Eugene of Savoy at Petrovaradin and Belgrade; ended by the Treaty of Passarowitz. Venice fought alongside Austria in the Morea and Corfu.

name: Austro-Russian–Turkish War (1735–1739)
description: Russian and Habsburg war against the Ottomans; Austria lost Belgrade by the Treaty of Belgrade.

name: Austro-Turkish War (1788–1791)
description: Joseph II's war against the Ottomans alongside Catherine the Great's Russia, ended by the Treaty of Sistova.

name: Austro-Hungarian occupation of Bosnia (1878)
description: Austro-Hungarian campaign to occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina under the Treaty of Berlin, resisted by local Muslim and Serb forces.

name: Transylvanian and Wallachian wars (1575–1611)
description: Dynastic and anti-Ottoman wars in Transylvania, Wallachia and Moldavia, including the campaigns of Michael the Brave.

name: Anglo-Norman succession wars
description: Wars among William the Conqueror's sons and their heirs for England and Normandy, decided at Tinchebray (1106).

name: Revolt of 1173–1174
description: Rebellion of Henry II's sons and Eleanor of Aquitaine, backed by France, Scotland and Flanders.

name: Anglo-Norman invasion of Ireland
description: Cambro-Norman intervention in Leinster followed by Henry II's expedition and the Treaty of Windsor.

name: William of Normandy's consolidation wars
description: Wars by which Duke William secured Normandy, from Val-ès-Dunes to Varaville.

name: Polish–Ottoman War (1672–1676)
description: Ottoman conquest of Podolia and Sobieski's victories at Khotyn and Lwów, ended by the Treaty of Żurawno.

name: Eastern Islamic dynastic wars (990–1120)
description: Wars among the Samanids, Ghaznavids, Karakhanids, Buyids and Seljuks for Khurasan, Transoxiana and Persia.

name: Wars of the Seljuk Empire
aliases: Wars of the Great Seljuk Sultanate
description: Seljuk conquest of Persia and the Middle East and the later wars of the Great Seljuk sultans.

name: Wars of the Second Bulgarian Empire
description: Wars of the restored Bulgarian state against Byzantium, the Latin Empire, Hungary and Serbia until the Ottoman conquest.

name: Mughal–Uzbek wars
description: Wars of Babur and his Mughal successors against the Shaybanid and Janid Uzbeks for Transoxiana, Kandahar and Balkh.

name: Medieval German civil wars (1018–1141)
description: Rebellions and succession wars in the Holy Roman Empire under the Salian and early Hohenstaufen kings, including the Saxon revolts.

name: Wars of East Francia and the Ottonians
description: Wars of the East Frankish and Ottonian kings against the Magyars, Slavs and rebellious dukes.

name: Hungarian invasions of Europe
description: Magyar raids into Germany, Italy and France, ended by Otto I's victory at Lechfeld.

name: Wars of the Neo-Assyrian Empire
description: Campaigns of the Neo-Assyrian kings from Adad-nirari II to the fall of Nineveh.

name: First Serbian Uprising
description: Serbian revolt against Ottoman rule led by Karađorđe, crushed in 1813.

name: Serbian–Ottoman Wars (1876–1878)
description: Serbia and Montenegro's wars against the Ottoman Empire during the Great Eastern Crisis.

name: Serbo-Bulgarian War
description: Serbia's brief war against Bulgaria after the unification with Eastern Rumelia, won by Bulgaria at Slivnitsa.

name: Wars of Stefan Dušan
description: Serbian expansion into Macedonia, Albania and Greece under Stefan Dušan.

name: Swabian War
description: War between the Swiss Confederacy and the Swabian League and Habsburgs, securing Swiss de facto independence.

name: Franco-Spanish War (1635–1659)
description: French war against Habsburg Spain begun during the Thirty Years' War and ended by the Peace of the Pyrenees.

name: War of the Reunions
description: Louis XIV's short war against Spain and the Empire to enforce his annexations, ended by the Truce of Ratisbon.

name: French invasion of Spain (1823)
description: The 'Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis' restored Ferdinand VII's absolute rule, ending the Liberal Triennium.

name: War of the Quadruple Alliance
description: Spain's attempt to recover Sardinia and Sicily, defeated by Britain, France, Austria and the Dutch Republic.

name: Roman–Vandal wars (455–468)
description: Vandal sack of Rome and the failed Roman expeditions against Gaiseric's Carthage, culminating in the disaster at Cape Bon.

name: Kaidu–Kublai war
description: War between Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty and Kaidu of the Ögedeid line for control of the Mongol Empire.

name: Rus'–Golden Horde wars
description: Wars of the Rus' principalities against the Golden Horde, from Blue Waters and Kulikovo to the Great Stand on the Ugra.

name: Mongol invasions of India
description: Repeated Mongol and Chagatai invasions of the Delhi Sultanate, repulsed by the Mamluk and Khalji sultans.

name: Corinthian War
description: War of Athens, Thebes, Corinth and Argos, backed by Persia, against Sparta, ended by the King's Peace.

name: Theban–Spartan War
aliases: Wars of the Greek City States
description: Thebes' war against Spartan hegemony, won at Leuctra and ended at Mantinea.

name: Third Sacred War
description: War of the Amphictyonic League and Philip II of Macedon against Phocis.

name: Lamian War
description: Greek revolt against Macedon after Alexander's death, defeated at Crannon.

name: Chremonidean War
description: Athens' and Sparta's war against Antigonid Macedon with Ptolemaic support.

name: Cleomenean War
description: War of Cleomenes III of Sparta against the Achaean League and Macedon, ended at Sellasia.

name: Sicilian Wars (Greek–Punic)
description: Three centuries of war between Carthage and the Greek cities of Sicily, chiefly Syracuse.

name: Roman conquest of Britain
description: Roman conquest of Britain from the Claudian invasion to Agricola's campaigns in Caledonia.

name: Caesar's invasions of Britain
description: Julius Caesar's two expeditions across the Channel during the Gallic Wars.

name: Early imperial campaigns in Germania
description: Roman campaigns beyond the Rhine under Augustus and Tiberius, including the Teutoburg disaster and Germanicus's wars.

name: Roman–Alemannic wars
description: Wars between Rome and the Alemanni on the Rhine and Danube frontiers, including Julian's victory at Strasbourg.

name: Second Samnite War
description: Rome's long war against the Samnites, including the humiliation at the Caudine Forks.

name: Third Samnite War
description: Final Samnite war, decided at Sentinum.

name: Roman–Etruscan Wars
description: Wars between Rome and the Etruscan city-states, from Veii to the conquest of Volsinii.

name: Roman–Seleucid war
description: Rome's war against Antiochus III, won at Thermopylae and Magnesia.

name: Medo-Babylonian conquest of Assyria
description: Babylonian and Median campaigns that destroyed the Neo-Assyrian Empire, including the fall of Nineveh.

name: Greco-Turkish War (1897)
description: Thirty Days' War over Crete, in which the Ottomans quickly defeated Greece in Thessaly.

name: Attila's Balkan campaigns
description: Hunnic invasions of the Eastern Roman Balkans that sacked Sirmium, Naissus and other cities.

name: Huguenot rebellions
description: Rebellions of the French Protestants under Louis XIII, ended by the fall of La Rochelle and the Peace of Alès.

name: Richard I's war with Philip II
description: Richard the Lionheart's war to recover his Norman and Angevin lands from Philip Augustus.

name: Ahmad Shah Durrani's campaigns
description: Campaigns of the founder of the Durrani Empire in Khurasan, Punjab and northern India, including the Third Battle of Panipat.

name: North-West Rebellion
description: Métis and Cree rising in Saskatchewan led by Louis Riel, defeated at Batoche.

name: Time of Troubles
description: Russian interregnum of famine, civil war, pretenders and Polish and Swedish intervention.

name: Pugachev's Rebellion
description: Cossack and peasant revolt on the Volga and Urals against Catherine the Great.

name: Franco-Flemish wars (1297–1328)
description: Wars between France and the County of Flanders, from the Golden Spurs to the Peasant revolt crushed at Cassel.

name: Wars of the Burgundian State
description: Wars of the Valois dukes of Burgundy against Ghent, Liège and France, ending in the Burgundian Wars.

name: Burgundian Wars
description: Charles the Bold's war against the Swiss and Lorraine, ending with his death at Nancy.

name: Portuguese colonial wars in Asia
aliases: Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
Later Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
Later Portuguese Colonial Wars in Arabia
description: Wars of the Portuguese Estado da Índia against Indian, Arabian, Malay and Ottoman powers, from Calicut and Diu to the loss of Hormuz and Cochin.

name: Avar–Byzantine wars
description: Wars between the Avar Khaganate (with Slavic allies) and the Byzantine Empire in the Balkans, ending with the failed siege of Constantinople.

name: Byzantine–Norman wars
description: Norman invasions of the Byzantine Balkans under Robert Guiscard, Bohemond and William II of Sicily.

name: Nicaean–Latin wars
description: Wars between the Empire of Nicaea and the Latin Empire of Constantinople, ending with the Byzantine recovery of the city. Later Byzantine campaigns against the Latin Principality of Achaea (1263–1264) are included.

name: Tang dynasty military campaigns
description: Frontier and internal wars of the Tang dynasty against the Turks, Tibetans, Nanzhao and rebellious governors.

name: Transition from Sui to Tang
description: Civil wars in which Li Yuan and Li Shimin overthrew the Sui and defeated rival warlords to found the Tang.

name: Wars of the Delhi Sultanate
description: Wars of expansion, succession and defence of the Delhi Sultanate until its fall to Babur at Panipat.

name: Mughal–Safavid wars
description: Recurrent Mughal–Safavid wars for Kandahar.

name: Safavid–Uzbek wars
description: Wars between Safavid (later Afsharid) Persia and the Shaybanid and Janid Uzbeks for Khurasan and Transoxiana.

name: Safavid–Aq Qoyunlu wars
description: Wars of the Safavid order under Haydar and Ismail I against the Aq Qoyunlu Turkomans, ending in the Safavid conquest of Persia.

name: Civil wars of the conquistadors in Peru
description: Wars among the Spanish conquerors of Peru (Pizarro, Almagro, Gonzalo Pizarro, Hernández Girón) and the Crown.

name: Dominican War of Independence
description: Dominican Republic's war of independence from Haiti and repulse of later Haitian invasions.

name: Filibuster War
description: Central American coalition war against William Walker's filibuster regime in Nicaragua.

name: War of Canudos
description: Brazilian army's destruction of the millenarian settlement of Canudos in Bahia.

name: Barbary corsair wars
description: European naval expeditions and bombardments against the corsair states of Algiers, Tunis, Tripoli and Salé.

name: Anglo-Welsh wars
description: Wars between the Welsh principalities and the English kings and Marcher lords, ending with Edward I's conquest.

name: Glyndŵr rebellion
description: Welsh revolt against Henry IV led by Owain Glyndŵr.

name: Kalmar War
description: Danish–Swedish war over the Kalmar Union's legacy and the northern trade routes.

name: Thirteen Years' War (1454–1466)
description: War of the Prussian Confederation and Poland against the Teutonic Order, ended by the Second Peace of Thorn.

name: First Schleswig War
description: War between Denmark and the Schleswig-Holstein rebels backed by Prussia and the German Confederation.

name: Swiss peasant war of 1653
description: Peasant revolt in the Swiss cantons of Lucerne, Bern, Solothurn and Basel.

name: War of the League of Cambrai
aliases: War of the League of Cambrai
y War of the Holy League
description: Italian War of 1508–1516 involving the Papacy, France, Venice, Spain and the Swiss.

name: Williamite War in Ireland
description: War between the Jacobite supporters of James II and the forces of William III in Ireland, decided at the Boyne and Aughrim.

name: Monmouth Rebellion
description: Duke of Monmouth's attempt to overthrow James II, crushed at Sedgemoor.

name: Prayer Book Rebellion
description: Revolt in Devon and Cornwall against the Book of Common Prayer.

name: Scottish clan wars
description: Feuds and battles among the Highland and Border clans of Scotland.

name: Lordship of the Isles rebellions
description: Wars of the MacDonald Lords of the Isles against the Scottish crown, from Harlaw to the forfeiture of the Lordship.

name: Early Scottish dynastic wars
description: Succession wars among the kings of Alba and Scotland, including the reign of Macbeth.

name: Covenanter risings
description: Presbyterian risings in south-west Scotland against the Restoration church settlement (Pentland Rising, Drumclog, Bothwell Bridge).

name: Frankish civil war (715–718)
description: Civil war after the death of Pepin of Herstal, won by Charles Martel.

name: Frankish–Burgundian wars
description: Wars by which the Merovingian Franks conquered the Kingdom of the Burgundians.

name: Nine Years' War (Ireland)
description: Hugh O'Neill's war against English rule in Ireland, ended after Kinsale by the Treaty of Mellifont.

name: Hungarian–Romanian War
description: Romania's war against the Hungarian Soviet Republic, ending with the occupation of Budapest.

name: Latvian War of Independence
description: Latvia's war against Soviet Russia, the Baltic Germans and the West Russian Volunteer Army.

name: Estonian War of Independence
description: Estonia's war against Soviet Russia and the Baltic German Landeswehr.

name: Lithuanian Wars of Independence
description: Lithuania's wars against the Soviets, the Bermontians and Poland.

name: Muscovite–Lithuanian Wars
description: Series of wars in which Muscovy took Chernigov, Smolensk and other lands from the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

name: Russo-Kazan Wars
description: Wars between Muscovy and the Khanate of Kazan, ended by Ivan IV's conquest of Kazan.

name: Montenegrin–Ottoman wars (1852–1862)
description: Ottoman campaigns against Montenegro under Omar Pasha, including Grahovac (1858).

name: Jebel Akhdar War
description: Revolt of the Imamate of Oman against the Sultan of Muscat, defeated with British help.

name: Iraqi revolt of 1920
description: Nationwide uprising against the British Mandate in Iraq.

name: Chitral Expedition
description: British relief of the besieged fort at Chitral on the North-West Frontier.

name: Waziristan campaign (1919–1920)
description: British-Indian campaign against the Wazir and Mahsud tribes after the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

name: Anglo-Nepalese War
description: War between the East India Company and the Kingdom of Nepal, ended by the Treaty of Sugauli.

name: Conquest of Sindh
description: Charles Napier's conquest of the Talpur emirs of Sindh at Miani and Hyderabad.

name: Gwalior campaign
description: British defeat of the Gwalior army at Maharajpur and Punniar.

name: Afghan–Sikh wars
description: Wars between the Durrani Afghans and the Sikh misls and Sikh Empire for the Punjab and Peshawar.

name: Persian Gulf campaigns (1809–1821)
description: British expeditions against the Qawasim of Ras al-Khaimah and the tribes of Oman, leading to the General Maritime Treaty of 1820.

name: Aden Expedition
description: British capture of Aden from the Sultan of Lahej.

name: Maratha–Bijapur wars
description: Shivaji's wars against the Adil Shahi sultanate of Bijapur, including Pratapgad and the conquest of the Konkan.

name: Mexican civil wars of the early republic
description: Federalist–centralist civil wars and pronunciamientos of the first Mexican republic.

name: Revolution of Tuxtepec
description: Porfirio Díaz's revolt against President Lerdo de Tejada, won at Tecoac.

name: Republic of Texas frontier conflicts
description: Wars of the Republic of Texas against the Cherokee and Comanche and the Mexican incursions and expeditions of 1842.

name: Cayuse War
description: War between the Cayuse and American settlers in Oregon after the Whitman massacre.

name: Ridda Wars
description: Campaigns of Abu Bakr against the Arab tribes that renounced Islam after Muhammad's death.

name: First Fitna
description: First Muslim civil war, between Ali and his opponents (Aisha, Talha, Zubayr and Mu'awiya).

name: Second Fitna
description: Second Muslim civil war after the death of Mu'awiya, including Karbala and the caliphate of Ibn al-Zubayr.

name: Third Fitna
description: Umayyad civil war and the Abbasid Revolution that overthrew the dynasty.

name: Carausian revolt
description: Usurpation of Carausius and Allectus in Britain, ended by Constantius Chlorus.

name: Gothic War (376–382)
description: Revolt of the Gothic refugees in Thrace, which destroyed Valens's army at Adrianople.

name: Ostrogothic conquest of Italy
description: Theodoric the Great's conquest of Odoacer's Italy.

name: Appenzell Wars
description: Revolt of Appenzell against the Abbey of St Gall and the Habsburgs.

name: Anglo-Spanish War (1625–1630)
description: War between Charles I's England and Spain, opened by the failed Cádiz expedition.

name: Anglo-Spanish War (1654–1660)
description: Cromwell's war against Spain, in which England took Jamaica and Dunkirk.

name: Anglo-Spanish War (1727–1729)
description: Spain's unsuccessful siege of Gibraltar and the British blockade of Porto Bello.

name: Ingrian War
description: Swedish intervention in Russia's Time of Troubles, ended by the Treaty of Stolbovo.

name: Russo-Swedish War (1656–1658)
description: Russia's attempt to gain a Baltic port during the Second Northern War.

name: Russo-Swedish War (1788–1790)
description: Gustav III's war against Russia, marked by the naval battles of Hogland and Svensksund.

name: Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)
description: War in which Russia and its Balkan allies defeated the Ottomans, leading to the independence of Romania, Serbia and Montenegro and an autonomous Bulgaria.

name: Rebellions of 1837–1838
description: Risings in Lower and Upper Canada against British colonial rule.

name: Liberal Wars
description: Portuguese civil war between the liberal supporters of Maria II and the absolutist Miguel I.

name: Fronde
description: Civil wars in France against Mazarin's regency during the minority of Louis XIV.

name: Genkō War
description: Civil war in which Emperor Go-Daigo overthrew the Kamakura shogunate.

name: Aragonese conquest of Naples
description: Alfonso V of Aragon's conquest of the Kingdom of Naples and the later suppression of the barons' revolt.

name: Ottoman invasion of Otranto
description: Ottoman capture of Otranto in southern Italy and its recovery by the Neapolitans.

name: Unification of Saudi Arabia
description: Wars by which Ibn Saud conquered Riyadh, Hasa, Ha'il, the Hejaz and Asir from the Rashidis, Hashemites and others to form Saudi Arabia.

name: Ikhwan revolt
description: Rebellion of the Ikhwan tribal militias against Ibn Saud, crushed at Sabilla.

name: Afghan Civil War (1928–1929)
